help.title: Help
help.collections_body: Your entries live in collections, and you look at one at a time. The button next to the collection's name opens its panel: type a name under New collection and press + to create one, or pick another from the list. Rename or delete the open collection there too; deleting it deletes its entries and photographs.
help.entries_body: New entry adds an entry to the open collection: a title and, if you like, a description, a place and tags. The buttons at the bottom of each entry add a photograph, edit the entry or delete it. Click a photograph to see it full size.
help.search_body: The search field looks through titles, descriptions, places and tags once you have typed three characters. The map button shows every entry whose place you picked from the suggestions.
help.sharing_body: In the collection's panel, under Sharing, enter someone's email to give their Google account access to the open collection; there are no public links. They can look at it, and with Can edit they can also add, change and delete entries and photographs. Renaming, deleting and sharing the collection stay with you.
help.transfer_body: In the collection's panel, Export saves the open collection as a .zip archive with all its photographs. Import turns such an archive into a new collection.
help.undo_body: Deleted an entry, a photograph or a collection by mistake? For a few seconds, Undo in the message at the bottom of the screen, or Ctrl+Z, brings it back. Ctrl+/ opens this help and Escape closes it. On a Mac, use Cmd instead of Ctrl.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.intro: CollectionBuddy stores the collections, entries and photos you add and lets you share a collection with other people. This notice explains which personal data that involves, why, who receives it, how long it is kept and which rights you have.
privacy.controller_text: The controller under the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and your contact for everything in this notice, is:
privacy.data_heading: What CollectionBuddy processes, and where it comes from
privacy.data_account: you sign in with Google. Google passes on your email address, your name, the address of your profile picture and your Google account ID, which are stored with your account. The app itself shows only your email address.
privacy.data_sign_ins: the time of each sign-in, and the IP address and browser a sign-in comes from.
privacy.data_collections: what you enter: the names of your collections and each entry's title, description, place and tags, with the times they were created and changed. A place you pick from the suggestions is stored with its coordinates.
privacy.data_photos: the photos you add. Your browser makes a reduced copy and a thumbnail before uploading them, and that drops the data embedded in the photo (EXIF), including any GPS position. A photo in an archive you import is stored exactly as it is in the archive. CollectionBuddy does not read embedded photo data.
privacy.data_sharing: when you share a collection, the email address you invite, whether that person may view or edit, and an expiry date if you set one. If someone shares a collection with you, they entered your email address.
privacy.data_location: the place names you type, which are looked up as described below. If you ask the map to show where you are, your browser determines your position, with your permission. It is used only on your screen and is neither stored nor sent to CollectionBuddy.
privacy.data_technical: your IP address, browser details and the time of each request, which every service below processes when your browser contacts it.
privacy.purpose_heading: Why, and on which legal basis
privacy.purpose_service: To provide the service you signed up for: your account, storing your collections and photos, showing them to you and to the people you share them with, place search, the map, export and import (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR, performance of a contract).
privacy.purpose_sharing: To store the email address of someone you share a collection with, so that they get access when they sign in (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR, our and your legitimate interest in sharing a collection).
privacy.purpose_security: To keep the service secure and available, for example against abuse (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR, legitimate interests).
privacy.purpose_required: You need a Google account to sign in; without one, CollectionBuddy cannot be used.
privacy.purpose_none: CollectionBuddy shows no advertising, uses no tracking and no analytics, does not sell your data or use it for anything else, and makes no automated decisions about you.
privacy.recipients_supabase: (Supabase, Inc.) runs the database, the photo storage and the sign-in for us, in Amazon Web Services' Frankfurt region (Germany), and processes all the data above on our behalf.
privacy.recipients_google: (Google Ireland Limited) handles the sign-in. Google learns that you sign in to CollectionBuddy; Google's own privacy policy applies to your Google account.
privacy.recipients_github: (GitHub, Inc., a Microsoft company) hosts this website on GitHub Pages and sees your IP address when your browser loads it.
privacy.recipients_photon: runs Photon (photon.komoot.io), which turns place names into coordinates. When you type a place, or open the map for places typed without picking a suggestion, your browser sends the place name, the language and your IP address to Photon. No account data is sent.
privacy.recipients_osm: serves the map images (tile.openstreetmap.org). Your browser loads them for the area you are looking at, which shows the OpenStreetMap Foundation your IP address and that area. The map data comes from OpenStreetMap.
privacy.recipients_people: see the shared collection with its entries and photos, and what you add to a collection shared with you is visible to others with access to it. The owner of a collection sees the email addresses invited to it.
privacy.recipients_transfer: Supabase, Google and GitHub belong to groups based in the United States, and they or their subcontractors may process data there. Such transfers rely on the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework or on the EU standard contractual clauses (Art. 45 and 46 GDPR). The OpenStreetMap Foundation is based in the United Kingdom, for which the EU has an adequacy decision.
privacy.retention_until_deleted: Your collections, entries and photos are kept until you delete them. After you delete something, the app lets you undo it for a few seconds; then it is removed from the database and the photo storage. There is no recycle bin.
privacy.retention_orphans: Photo files left behind by an interrupted upload or deletion are removed automatically after 48 hours.
privacy.retention_account: Your account is kept until you delete it: "Delete account" in the account menu deletes it with all your collections, entries and photos, the shares you made and the shares made to you. You can also write to the contact above. Photos you added, as an editor of a shared collection, to its owner's entries belong to those entries and stay with them.
privacy.retention_sharing: An invitation is kept until the owner or the invited person removes it, or the collection is deleted, even after its expiry date has passed.
privacy.retention_logs: Supabase keeps its technical logs, with IP addresses, for one day and its sign-in logs for one hour. Records of your sign-ins can also be kept with your account while it exists. GitHub, Google, Komoot and the OpenStreetMap Foundation keep their own logs under their own policies.
privacy.browser_heading: What is stored in your browser
privacy.browser_storage: CollectionBuddy keeps your sign-in session, your language, your colour theme, the collection you last opened and the coordinates the map has looked up for place names in your browser's local storage, so they survive a reload. It also notes which account the last collection and the coordinates belong to, and removes both when a different account signs in on the same browser. For the open tab, it records when it last reloaded itself after an update.
privacy.browser_cache: A service worker keeps a copy of the app's own files so that it starts faster and opens offline; it keeps none of your collections or photos.
privacy.browser_no_cookies: CollectionBuddy sets no cookies and uses no tracking. What it stores is needed for the service you asked for (Section 25(2) no. 2 TDDDG).
privacy.rights_in_app: You can see, correct and delete your collections, entries and photos in the app at any time, export each collection as a ZIP archive, and delete your account.
privacy.rights_list: You have the right of access (Art. 15 GDPR), rectification (Art. 16), erasure (Art. 17), restriction of processing (Art. 18) and data portability (Art. 20), and the right to object to processing based on legitimate interests (Art. 21). To exercise any of these rights, write to the contact above.
privacy.rights_complaint: You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority, in particular in the EU member state where you live or work or where you believe the infringement took place (Art. 77 GDPR).
